full_judgment:
3. Facts for the disposal of this Rule are that, Hazera Khanam and Mst. Juberia Khanam as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 243 of 82 in the Court of 1st Munsif, Sadar Sylhet for declaration of their absolute and unrestricted right of way over the schedule pathway and for a permanent injunction restraining the defendant No. 1 from interfering with the plaintiffs' absolute and unrestricted right of way over the schedule pathway. Plaintiff stated in the plaint that plaintiffs and defendant belong to same stock. Mufti Abdul Quadir was their remote predecessor-in-interest, who died leaving two sons namely, Mufti Bashiruddin and Mufti Mohiuddin. Then Mufti Bashiruddin died leaving two sons Mufti Mesbahuddin, the defendant No. 2, and Mufti Jainuddin, Mufti Jainuddin died leaving a widow, the plaintiff No. 1, a daughter the plaintiff No. 2 and 4 sons, the pre-defendants Nos. 3-6 as his heirs. Mufti Mohiuddin died leaving only son Mufti AM Jalaluddin, the principal defendant No. 1, plaintiffs and defendants were enjoying ejmali properties. During the last survey and settlement operation, their email properties were recorded in a joint Khatian comprising SS plot Nos. 4604, 4605 and 4608 having a total area of 1.15 decimals of land. Out of these, SS plot No. 4604 was shown under possession of Mufti Mesbahuddin and others including the plaintiffs and pro-defendant Nos. 3-6, the heirs of Mufti Bashiruddin. Whereas SS plot No. 4605 was shown to be under the possession of Mufti AM Jalaluddin alone and SS plot No. 4608 was shown under joint possession in the joint names of the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 1 to 6. But there was no partition among the parties by metes and bounds. For the sake of convenience the plaintiff and proforma-defendant Nos. 2-6 had been owning and possessing the land of SS plot No. 4604 in ejmali including the principal defendant No. 1, whereas, the principal defendant No. 1 alone had been owning and possessing the land of SS plot No. 4605 exclusively. The land of SS plot No. 4608 was being owned and possessed by the plaintiffs and the defendants in ejmali. The plaintiffs and the defendants Nos. 3-6 were residing in the northern most portion of SS Plot No. 4604 and they had been enjoying the land of the SS plot No. 4608 in ejmali with defendant Nos. 1-6 and they had been using the pathway described in the schedule of the suit openly, peaceably, uninterruptedly and unrestrictedly, as of right, without any let or hindrance from any quarter, from the time of their remote predecessor. They claimed that they acquired indefeasible easement right over the suit property and the plaintiffs and the defendants were also owners of the land of the suit pathway. The plaintiffs and defendants had earlier filed Title Suit No. 361 of 66, for another private pathway of their own. The suit pathway was relaid by a local investigateting Commissioner. The local investigating commissioner found the existence of suit pathway. The Suit pathway was being used by the plaintiffs and the defendants for their absolute necessity. The plaintiff No. 1 was a helpless widow while plaintiff No. 2 is her daughter and the pro-defendant Nos. 1-6 are her sons, plaintiff No. 2 mostly resides with her husband, while pro-defendant Nos. 3-6 are residing abroad and taking advantage of the helpless condition of the plaintiffs, the principal defendant No. 1 chalked out a plan to increase and augment quantum of his land lying to the west of the suit pathway, and with this end in view had been creating troubles in the use and enjoyment of the suit pathway smoothly by plaintiffs and the pro-defendants. They had no other alternative pathway accepting the suit pathway to link up with the main road connecting, the Dargah-e-Hazrat Shah Jalal to the west and the Sylhet Airport road to east. The defendant No. 1 was a litigant by nature and he got many designing persons at his beck and call and unless he was restrained by an order of temporary injunction, with ad-interim order from interfering with suit pathway till disposal of the suit, the plaintiffs and the pro-defendants would be confined to their respective houses, and thereby, they would suffer irreparable loss and injury. The suit was amended and a prayer for mandatory injunction for a direction on the principal defendant to dismantle and remove the wall and all other obstructions from the suit pathway within a time specified was made. 

 8. I have heard the learned Advocates of the parties at length, perused the plaint, written statement and exhibits, evidence of the plaintiffs and defendant, and both the judgments of the courts below. It appears that the plaintiff's suit is for declaration of their absolute right of way over the suit property, and for a decree for permanent injunction. The plaintiffs stated in the plaint that plaintiffs and defendants were of same stock. The suit property belonged to Abdul Kadir, who was a remote predecessor-in-interest of the parties. The plaintiffs and the defendant were joint owners of the property measuring 1.52 acres under a joint khatian comprised of SS plot No. 4604, 4605 and 4608. Plaintiffs and the defendant were in possession of the property for convenience. The property was not partitioned among them by metes and bounds. It is stated that for the convenience of possession the plaintiffs and pro-defendants are owning and possessing SS plot No. 4604 in ejmali excluding principal defendant No. 1. The principal defendant No. 1 alone has been owning and possessing the land of SS plot No. 4605 exclusively, while the land of SS plot No. 4608 is being owned and possessed by the plaintiffs and the defendant in ejmali. Defendant No. 1 stated in his written statement that there was an amicable partial partition among the heirs of Mufti Basiruddin and Mufti Mohiuddin. The heirs of Mufti got the land comprising plot No. 4604 in their saham. The homestead is in plot No. 4608 and the path in plot No. 4607 remained in ejmali. The heirs of Mufti Mohiuddin got plot No. 4605 in their saham exclusively. Plaintiffs and defendants as plaintiffs earlier filed Title Suit No. 361 of 66, for an ejmali path in plot No. 4607, which was encroached upon by a grand-daughter of Mufti Nasiruddin. The suit was subsequently transferred to the Additional Court of Munsif and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 124 of 97. The defendant No. 1 stated that he had two pucca buildings and one semipucca building on the land of plot No. 4605. Same buildings are with frontage to the east. The defendant No. 1 had allowed the tenants of the building to use the vacant space in the eastern portion of plot No. 4605 as passage. In the written statement defendant No. 1 further stated that there was no document of partition and the plaintiff No. 1 and pro-defendant No. 2 executed a deed of relinquishment in respect of plot No. 4605. The plaintiffs cannot claim the right in the suit land as the suit land was never a pathway and the plaintiffs and defendants never used it and they have no right title in plot No. 4605 and their claim of right of way by easement or lost grant or otherwise is false. 

 10. From the averments made in the plaint, it shows that the properties of the plaintiffs, preformed defendants and the defendant No. 1 are the joint properties and they are in possession of the property under a joint Khatian. The property measures 1.15 decimal of land under plot Nos. 4604, 4605 and 4608. According to the plaint, for the sake of convenience, the plaintiffs and pro-defendants Nos. 2-6 have been owning SS Plot No. 4608 in ejmali including defendant No. 1, Defendant No. 1 alone possesses the plot No. 4605 exclusively, and the land SS plot No. 4604 is being owned and possessed by the plaintiffs. Whereas the defendant No. 1 admitted in written statement that earlier a suit was filed by the defendant and plaintiffs and that there was no document of partition and for the sake of obtaining loan from House Building Finance Corporation a document of relinquishment of claim was made by the plaintiffs for the land in favour of the defendant No. 1. It appears that there was no final partition of the property among the plaintiffs and defendants, by metes and bounds. The possession of the plaintiffs and defendants in the property in their respective portion is for convenience of parties. The plaintiffs have claimed easement in the schedule property which belongs to all the parties to the suit, including the plaintiffs. By misreading Exhibit 'C', the deed of relinquishment, the court below took the Exhibit 'C' as a document of partition, and decreed the suit. The court of appeal below also misconstrued the Exhibit C and found same deed to be a 'specific partition' and decreed the suit. The findings of both the courts below on the basis of Exhibit 'C' are erroneous. It is abundantly clear from the plaint that there was no partition of the property among the plaintiffs and the defendants. The Khatian was prepared in joint names and the possession of the plaintiffs and defendants were for convenience in the absence of any partition by metes and bounds. The defendant No. 1 admitted in his written statement that there was no deed of partition and the Exhibit 'C' was executed between plaintiffs and defendant No. 1 for obtaining a loan from the House Building Finance Corporation. The Exhibit 'C' is on record. It is a Photostat copy. It was executed by Md Mezbauddin and Hazera Khatun. This Exhibit 'C' cannot be treated as document of partition, because the property was not owned by Mezbauddin and Hazera only. There are some other owners of the property. Partition is a division made between the several persons of joint land. By the document Exhibit 'C' no portion was divided and all the co-sharers are not party in this document. Thus, it appears that the plaintiffs are also owners of the suit land and they cannot claim right of easement on the property of their own. The learned Senior Advocate Mr Huq has submitted strenuously that the concurrent findings of the courts below are that the property is under the exclusive possession of defendant No. 1 as his own property, and these findings cannot be interfered with by this Court and that it has been proved that there was an amicable partition once and no suit for partition is maintainable, and he cited the case of Halim Khatun vs Hamid Mia reported in 10 BLC 1.
